$comment: A hiring manager for a water utility and one for an AI governance team are
looking for different things, and both currently get the same undifferentiated
list of six projects in reverse-chronological order. A lens reorders the
portfolio around one of them and says, in one paragraph, what the through-line
is — without hiding anything: every lens still shows every case study, the
non-matching ones simply move below a divider.
That constraint is deliberate. A view that silently drops the projects it
finds inconvenient is a CV that lies by omission. These reorder and frame;
Each lens id names its own generated page — case-studies-water.html, and so
on. That is deliberate: an earlier version selected the lens client-side from
?lens=water, which cannot work on a static host, so every shared link showed
the default view while the README claimed otherwise. A static page per lens
needs no JavaScript at all, and these pages ship none.
Renaming a lens id therefore renames a URL. Do it only with a reason, and
update index.html, field-report.html and the README in the same commit —
tests/portfolio.test.js checks that every lens link points at a page that
exists, and that nothing has drifted back to the ?lens= form.

default.label: Everything
default.summary: Six projects across four countries, joined by one question: what does the data actually say, and who is it for? Water first, then climate risk, now the footprint of the tools themselves.

lenses.label: Water resources & WASH
lenses.tagline: From the drill bit to the river mouth
lenses.summary: I started underground. A geology degree, then electrical-resistivity surveying to find water in hard rock, then drilling crews delivering 164 water points across Sierra Leone. Later the same question at basin scale: what reaches the coast, and who put it there. The through-line is that water problems are rarely only hydraulic — the borehole that works is the one the community can maintain.
lenses.bestFor: Roles in water resource management, WASH programming, hydrogeology, or utility planning — especially where field delivery and analysis have to meet.
evidence: 164 water points delivered — 100 wells rehabilitated, 50 boreholes, 14 solar-powered
70% aquifer strike rate against roughly 30% for blind siting
10,226 sub-basins modelled for river pollution export
MSc thesis proposing soft-path alternatives to hard water infrastructure

lenses.label: Climate adaptation & disaster risk
lenses.tagline: Planning for the year the river wins
lenses.summary: Disaster risk is a data problem before it is an engineering one — you cannot reduce what you cannot compare. At UNDRR that meant auditing Caribbean loss data and standardising the terminology behind it. In Wuppertal it meant asking a municipality what it would take to keep a suspended railway out of a flood, and turning climate projections into a roadmap somebody could act on.
lenses.bestFor: Roles in climate adaptation, disaster risk reduction, resilience planning, or climate-risk analysis — particularly where frameworks like Sendai, CSRD or TCFD are in play.
evidence: 54 global hazard information systems documented for UNDRR
Caribbean disaster-loss data audited for the Sendai Framework Monitor
National risk-management factsheet for Trinidad and Tobago
Six-person flood-resilience consultancy for the Municipality of Wuppertal

lenses.label: Sustainable AI & AI governance
lenses.summary: The newest thread, and the one that made the rest make sense: the tools we now use to analyse environmental problems have environmental costs of their own, and almost nobody is measuring them. At the Digital Society School I am building the framework and the decision-support tooling for a finance ministry adopting generative AI — mapping Scope 2 electricity, Scope 3 hardware and data-centre water, in a reporting language the organisation already speaks.
lenses.bestFor: Roles in sustainable AI, AI governance, green software, or ESG where digital footprint is in scope — and anywhere the job is to make an environmental claim survive scrutiny.
evidence: Sustainable-AI framework and prototype for the Dutch Ministry of Finance
EcoPrompt Coach — a public tool with a full evidence ledger behind every factor
Framework framed against CSRD/ESRS disclosure logic
This site: a first view of ~235 KB, budgeted and enforced in CI
